{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — 18 findings

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. Nine of eighteen rules are met, including the items that usually cost us the most negotiating capital: the liability cap in Section 21.1 is mutual at the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 with a full set of Excluded Claims; assignment (Section 24), licence scope (Sections 13.1–13.3), audit (Section 22), renewal (Section 8), warranty (Section 19) and insurance (Section 18) all sit at our preferred positions.

The remaining nine findings are concentrated in two clusters. First, a set of one-sided restrictions on us: the three-year take-or-pay in Section 2.1, the disclose-and-match obligation in Section 7.2, and the twenty-four-month non-compete and no-hire in the two clauses both numbered 12.4. Each of these sits in walk-away territory under the playbook, and each contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor expressly acknowledges that we have given no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. Second, three gaps: there is no indemnification section at all (the numbering jumps from 19 to 21, while Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one and cross-refer to a non-existent "Section 20.5"), no Customer termination for convenience against a three-year term, and no transition-assistance or data-return obligation for a hosted service. We have also reversed the Deliverables assignment in Section 14.2 and aligned the governing law in Section 28.1 with New York, which Section 28.2 already specifies for venue.

The agreement carries several internal inconsistencies and dangling cross-references (missing Section 20, duplicate Section 12.4, Section 16.5 pointing to a non-existent Section 11, Section 28.1 conflicting with Section 28.2). These should be resolved in the same turn.

---

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | No indemnity section; numbering jumps 19 → 21 (see § 19.5) | No Vendor IP or other indemnity exists, yet §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 assume one and cross-refer to "Section 20.5". We have inserted our standard Vendor indemnity with notice/control procedure, infringement remedies and a narrow Customer indemnity. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor takes exclusive ownership of Deliverables built for us, with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence back — below the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable) and in tension with § 13.2. We reversed the assignment with a perpetual licence fallback; Vendor Technology stays with Vendor under § 14.3. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 | Preferred position met: mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, mutual consequential-damages exclusion (data restoration and replacement services preserved as direct damages), broad Excluded Claims, and § 18.2 confirming insurance does not limit Vendor's liability. |
| 4 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (second instance) | Undefined-scope, all-territory, twenty-four-month post-term non-compete on us — walk-away territory, and contradicted by § 12.3. Deleted. |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9.5 (termination provisions generally; term at § 8.1) | Three-year term with only for-cause, insolvency, security/service-level and force-majeure exits (§§ 9.1–9.5, 27.3); § 2.1 expressly denies termination rights. Walk-away. We inserted a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees. |
| 6 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Assignment to Affiliates and successors without consent; § 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and bars assignment to our competitors; § 24.4 removes any Vendor right on our change of control. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; § 12.3 preserves our freedom to engage any supplier. The match right in § 7.2 is addressed under MFN rather than flagged twice. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 | No liquidated damages, penalty or minimum termination charge; § 21.3 limits our payment obligation to undisputed Fees for conforming Services. The § 2.1 take-or-pay is addressed under MINCOMMIT. |
| 9 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 | Affiliates and contractors covered; paid-up and embedded software licensed perpetually and irrevocably; revocation limited to material uncured breach after notice and cure; rights transferable to an Affiliate or successor. The narrower Deliverable licence in § 14.2 is addressed under IP. |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right — walk-away, and contradicted by § 12.3. Narrowed to the fallback: current 12-month term only, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up instead of penalty. |
| 11 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | Open-ended obligation to disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer before engaging another provider — no scope limit, time limit or comparison carve-outs; walk-away, and inconsistent with § 12.3. Deleted; a Vendor-granted MFN remains welcome. |
| 12 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-sided twenty-four-month no-hire covering every Vendor employee with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out — walk-away, and inconsistent with § 12.3. Narrowed to a mutual 12-month non-solicit of personnel directly involved in the Services, with standard carve-outs and no no-hire. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue is outside our accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and conflicts with § 28.2, which gives exclusive jurisdiction to the New York County courts. Aligned to New York law and venue. |
| 14 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (and § 16.5, which defers to a non-existent Section 11) | Section 10 covers only access wind-down, Deliverable delivery and refunds; no transition assistance and no obligation to return or export Customer Data in a usable format. We inserted transition assistance, data return within 30 days and certified deletion. |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 | Once per twelve months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.1 (uplift at § 8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day Customer opt-out extended if Vendor misses its 60-day reminder, uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% on 90 days' notice. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.2 | 90-day Deliverable conformity plus term-long hosted Service conformity, professional and workmanlike performance, no malicious code, compliance with Applicable Law, re-perform/repair/replace with refund and termination if uncured; § 19.5 preserves the express warranties. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL USD 1M/2M, employer's liability USD 1M, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation, for the term plus one year, with certificates on request and § 18.2 confirming insurance does not cap liability. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following are identified in our findings as walk-away territory. Each has been redlined; we should not sign without resolution:

1. **No Vendor indemnity at all (missing Section 20).** With no IP indemnity, and with §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 cross-referring to provisions that do not exist, this is walk-away. Our standard Vendor indemnity has been inserted.
2. **No Customer termination for convenience (§§ 8.1, 9.1–9.5, 2.1).** A three-year term with no convenience exit, and § 2.1 expressly denying termination rights, is walk-away. We added a 30-day right with pro-rata refund.
3. **Three-year take-or-pay (§ 2.1).** USD 2,000,000 per year with no reduction or termination right. Narrowed to the 12-month fallback with a true-up.
4. **Customer-side MFN / match right (§ 7.2).** Unlimited scope, no time limit, no comparison carve-outs. Deleted.
5. **Twenty-four-month non-compete (§ 12.4, second instance).** Undefined scope, all territories, post-term. Deleted.
6. **Twenty-four-month no-hire (§ 12.4).** All Vendor employees, no carve-outs, one-sided. Narrowed to a mutual 12-month involved-personnel non-solicit.

We note that items 3 to 6 each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3 that we have given no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That inconsistency is our strongest argument for deletion and should be led with.

---

## Next steps

1. **Send the marked-up draft** with the six walk-away redlines, the § 14.2 ownership reversal, the § 28.1 governing-law alignment and the inserted transition/data-return paragraph, each tagged with the `[Playbook]` comment prefix and our position and fallback.
2. **Lead the call with § 12.3.** Ask Vendor to confirm which of §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4 it intends to keep given its own acknowledgement, and press for deletion of the rest as drafting residue.
3. **Require a clean renumbered draft** resolving the structural defects: the missing Section 20 and the dangling "Section 20.5" reference, the duplicate Section 12.4, the § 16.5 reference to a non-existent Section 11, and the § 28.1 / § 28.2 conflict.
4. **Confirm the fallbacks we can accept** before the negotiation: perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable Deliverable licence in place of ownership (§ 14.2); commitment limited to the current 12 months, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up (§ 2.1); mutual 12-month involved-personnel non-solicit with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs (§ 12.4).
5. **Hold the compliant clauses.** Sections 13, 18, 19, 21, 22 and 24 sit at our preferred positions; we should resist any reopening of the liability cap or licence scope as consideration for movement elsewhere.
6. **Escalate to the business owner** if Vendor declines on the indemnity or the convenience right, as neither has an acceptable fallback in the playbook."}
